recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No further core FHIR source work is needed for FHIR-31823 unless a future BRR decision reopens SubstanceDefinition categorization semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-31823 was a Published/Persuasive BRR change request for the R4 SubstanceSpecification artifact, applied for R5, asking to drop category and combine it with classification as a 0..* element.
initial_application: Commit 259da1896e7c0d38a4b4569da43d71619538ba10 explicitly applied "combined category and classification FHIR#31823" by removing SubstanceDefinition.category, keeping SubstanceDefinition.classification at 0..*, broadening its text to cover high-level and lower-level categorization, and changing the search parameter from category to classification.
additional_context: The active R5 build uses SubstanceDefinition rather than the old SubstanceSpecification name. source/fhir.ini actively lists substancedefinition=SubstanceDefinition and marks SubstanceDefinition approved. BRR minutes for 2021-06-15 placed FHIR-31823 into block vote 2, and no Zulip discussion was found that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/substancedefinition/structuredefinition-SubstanceDefinition.xml already has SubstanceDefinition.classification at max * with wording covering high-level and lower-level categorization, no SubstanceDefinition.category element remains, and the SubstanceDefinition search parameter bundle exposes classification rather than category.

related_jiras.note: The same historical source commit also changed SubstanceDefinition.relationship.type cardinality; that is a separate issue and was not decided here.
The same historical source commit also changed SubstanceDefinition.identifier cardinality; that is a separate issue and was not decided here.
